bullets.title: Mag-7 suffers -4.8% single-day selloff on AI capex/ROI concerns; GOOGL, TSLA lead the damage
bullets.body: The Magnificent 7 basket fell 4.8% in its biggest one-day decline in five years, losing $797B in combined market cap. GOOGL dropped 7.1% and broke its 200-day moving average for the first time in over a year after raising FY26 capex guidance by $15B to $195-205B, while TSLA plunged 14.5%—its worst day since March 2025—after management cautioned on unsupervised autonomy scale-up timelines. S&P 500 futures bounced +0.2% pre-market Friday, with Nasdaq flat.

bullets.title: Iran escalation pushes Brent above $100; US conducts 13th night of strikes; ceasefire rejected
bullets.body: Brent crude settled at $100.69/bbl (+7%), its highest since May, as the US conducted a 13th consecutive night of strikes on IRGC targets and Iran rejected a ceasefire proposal carried by Iraqi PM. Iranian FM warned of retaliation against regional energy infrastructure, and IRGC claimed destruction of an Amazon data center. Oil prices pulled back ~$1-2/bbl Friday morning on technical correction signals, with WTI at $91.20.

bullets.title: US imposes 10-12.5% Section 301 tariffs on 60 nations over forced labor; Section 122 expiry
bullets.body: New tariffs under Section 301 authority took effect July 24 at 12:01am ET, replacing the expiring 10% global Section 122 duty. Compliant nations pay 10%, non-compliant 12.5%, covering 99.4% of US imports. Oil, gas, fertilizer, foodstuffs, and USMCA-compliant goods are exempt. The EU expressed surprise at its inclusion; India is negotiating lower rates. Higher-rate 301 measures from broader excess-capacity investigations remain pending.

bullets.title: 10-year yields breach 4.7% for first time since Jan 2025; Japan bond yields hit multi-decade highs; Fed hike odds rise
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield surpassed 4.7% on oil-driven inflation fears, with markets now pricing ~40bp of tightening in 2026 and ~30-36% probability of a July FOMC hike (down slightly from 40%). The 30-year hit 5.18%, highest in 19 years. Japan's 5-year yield hit an all-time high of 2.045% and its 2-year reached a 30-year high of 1.505%. Morgan Stanley and Goldman both expect the Fed to hold in July but flag risks of resumed hikes later in 2026 if oil/inflation persist.

bullets.title: Intel posts strongest revenue growth in 15+ years; raises FY26 capex to $20B+
bullets.body: Intel Q2 revenue $16.13B (+25% YoY, beat of $14.4B consensus) with EPS $0.42 vs $0.22 estimate; DCAI surged 59% YoY to $6.3B on server CPU and agentic AI demand. Q3 guidance $15.8-16.8B and EPS $0.38, both well ahead of consensus. FY26 capex raised from $17B to $20B+ with 2027 expected 'significantly higher'; 18A yields running ~25% above targets; 14A committed for high-volume production in 2028. Stock pared early 11% after-hours gains to ~3% amid investor concerns over potential equity issuance and 14A being internal-only.

bullets.title: AMD AI Day: Helios in production, Anthropic/OpenAI wins, TAM raised to $1.4T by 2030
bullets.body: AMD launched Helios rack-scale AI platform (75 MI455X GPUs/rack, 31TB HBM4) with shipments beginning Sept 2026, ramping through 1H27. Anthropic committed to 2GW MI450 and AMD made a $5B equity investment; OpenAI and Meta each deploying 6GW. Server CPU TAM raised to $220B by 2030 (from $120B); AI accelerator TAM raised to $1.4T by 2030 (>45% CAGR). UBS and multiple analysts raised PTs to $700-$730; AMD Venice CPU beats NVIDIA Vera on single-core and throughput metrics.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex boom drives broad semi supply-chain upgrade; INTC/TSMC/GOOGL/TSLA all raised spend
bullets.body: Citi flagged the SOX selloff as a buying opportunity, noting data center at 34% of semi TAM is on track to exceed entire semi TAM by 2030. TSMC raised 2026 capex to $60-64B (from $56B); Google raised FY26 capex by $15B to $195-205B; Tesla exceeds $25B; Intel to $20B+. Consensus 2026/27 semi revenue estimates rose 4%/7%, EPS 7%/8%. Semi-cap equipment preferred over semis; DRAM supply-demand balance tightened with industry inventory at 2.6-2.7 weeks vs. 5-week normal.

bullets.title: Jefferies AI Bubble Bear Case: capex at 92% of OCF, token prices collapsing, Chinese open-source threat growing
bullets.body: Jefferies warned AI capex may be peaking with hyperscaler spending reaching 92% of operating cash flow in 2026. Chinese open-source models (DeepSeek, Kimi K3) pose growing competitive threat, LLM token prices are collapsing, and ~$2.1T in RPOs is essentially unsecured lending to cash-burning tenants. Oracle was downgraded to BBB- (near junk). The note drew parallels to late-1990s dot-com dynamics and Japanese 'zaitech' financial engineering, flagging the 10-year at 4.7% as a 'yellow signal.'

bullets.title: Eurozone July composite PMI surges to 51.9, well above 50.2 forecast; Germany and France both beat
bullets.body: Eurozone flash composite PMI rose 1.9pts to 51.9 in July, consistent with ~1.4% annualized GDP growth vs JPMorgan's 1% Q3 forecast. Germany hit 51.2 (vs 49.8 expected) and France rose to 49.6 (vs 47.8). ECB 1-year inflation expectations fell to 3.0% (vs 3.2% est.), though Middle East energy risks could reverse progress. The UK composite PMI also surged to 52.1, and retail sales beat with +4.2% YoY.

bullets.title: US initial jobless claims fall to lowest since 1969; labor market remains historically tight
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims hit their lowest level since 1969, signaling continued labor market tightness. The data reinforces the Fed's patient-but-watchful stance amid rising oil and yields.

bullets.title: Mag-7 defensive rotation underway; tech below 50-day MA; defensive sectors outperform
bullets.body: The S&P 500 closed below its 50-day moving average by the largest margin since April, with GOOGL breaking its 200-day MA for the first time in over a year. Piper notes defensive rotation into Industrials, Financials, Energy, Utilities, and Healthcare vs. Technology. AAII bullish sentiment collapsed 15 percentage points to 29.6% (below the 37.5% historical average); bearish sentiment rose to 42.3%. Retail buying remains near the 98th percentile vs. the 3-year prior, and hedge funds rebuilt ~60% of record de-grossing since May.

bullets.title: KOSPI plunges 5-6% on memory bear note, leveraged ETF regulatory crackdown
bullets.body: Seoul's KOSPI index fell 5.72-6% intraday with widespread trading halts, triggered in part by a Morgan Stanley analyst (Shawn Kim) turning bearish on memory chips and South Korea's government fast-tracking rules raising margin requirements for leveraged single-stock products. The selloff spread to Taiwan (-2%+) and Japan (Nikkei -3%), with Samsung Electronics down 6.5% and SK Hynix down 5%.

bullets.title: DLR record 2Q bookings, $1.4B backlog; data center demand structural and accelerating
bullets.body: Digital Realty reported record retail bookings of $108M in 0-1MW + interconnect in 2Q, plus $205M in hyperscale leases signed post-quarter. Backlog rose to $1.4B and FY26 guidance was raised for revenue, EBITDA, and FFO/share. Management guided to double-digit core FFO/share CAGR through 2028. JPMorgan raised PT to $235; UBS upgraded to Buy with $227 PT on 11% FFO/share CAGR 2026-28 and strong pricing outlook.

bullets.title: NVDA commits $1.5B to Amkor for US chip packaging; GPU residual value guarantees unlock bank financing
bullets.body: Nvidia signed a multi-year strategic partnership with Amkor Technology including $1.5B in prepayments for advanced semiconductor packaging and test in the US. Separately, analysis noted NVIDIA is offering residual value guarantees on GPUs to enable bank financing of AI clusters—a structural shift enabling speculative AI infrastructure to become bankable projects.

bullets.title: ORCL wins $7B Pentagon contract and $3.3B Navy deal; CRM wins $1.6B VA contract
bullets.body: Oracle signed a 10-year Pentagon software consolidation contract worth up to $7B and a separate $3.31B 5-year US Navy contract for perpetual and subscription software. Salesforce was awarded a $1.6B three-year VA contract for care and service delivery. Both stocks are pre-market gainers (+2.2% and +1.7% respectively).

bullets.title: Fed expected to hold at July FOMC; market pricing ~40bp of hikes for 2026; patience running thin
bullets.body: Consensus from Morgan Stanley, Goldman, and JPMorgan is for the Fed to hold rates at 3.50-3.75% at the July 29 FOMC meeting. However, the market is pricing ~40bp of tightening for 2026 and a 30-36% probability of a July hike—elevated by oil above $100 and strong labor data. Morgan Stanley warns the Fed will resume hikes later in 2026 if disinflation stalls.

bullets.title: Section 301 tariffs intensify: 10-12.5% on 60 nations creates pricing pressure; analysts flag upstream inflationary risk
bullets.body: With the new tariff regime now in effect, analysts note the broader risk of cost inflation across supply chains. Goldman flagged tariffs as re-emerging key focus, and Piper cited the regime now covering 99.4% of US imports at 10-12.5% with potential for higher rates from ongoing 301 investigations into excess capacity. If oil disruptions extend 2+ months, JPMorgan estimates gasoline could spike above $4.50/gallon, historically triggering geopolitical negotiations.

bullets.title: Memory cycle intact; NAND/DRAM supplier inventory at 2.6-2.7 weeks vs. 5-week normal
bullets.body: Citi reiterates Buy on Samsung and SK Hynix, arguing the memory upcycle remains intact on structurally lean inventories. NAND supplier inventory stands at 2.6 weeks vs. a normal 5 weeks, and hyperscaler DRAM inventory is at 2.5 weeks vs. a normal 7 weeks. AI inference and KV cache demand is driving CMX NAND and SOCAMM2 adoption; DRAM bit demand growth is forecast at 36% YoY in 2027 vs. 22% in 2026.

bullets.title: China: K-shaped growth persists; Beijing comfortable with weak domestic demand; strong stimulus unlikely
bullets.body: JPMorgan on-the-ground meetings found Beijing comfortable with export/tech strength offsetting weak consumption and is focused on industrial policy goals rather than demand-side stimulus. Strong stimulus is unlikely unless social stability is threatened or exports falter. China's tech confidence is growing despite US compute controls, and Taiwan conflict risk is viewed as low for the foreseeable future.

bullets.title: TSLA down 14.5% on autonomy scaling constraints; management cautions 40-vehicle threshold before broad unsupervised rollout
bullets.body: Tesla's worst day since March 2025 came after management signaled that unsupervised autonomy would not be broadly scaled until ~40 test vehicles demonstrated sufficient safety, with no specific metrics (paid rides/week, active unsupervised fleet) disclosed. Waymo currently operates 3,500 unsupervised vehicles and 500K paid rides/week vs. Tesla's ~40 vehicles and ~4K rides. Piper cut PT by $50 to $450; ARK bought 160K shares on the dip.
